purpose: Lithium carbonate is used to treat bipolar disorder, which causes extreme mood swings between highs (mania) and lows (depression). It helps reduce the intensity and frequency of manic episodes, such as feeling overly excited, impulsive, or irritable. It can also help prevent future mood episodes when taken regularly.
how_it_works: Lithium works by balancing certain natural chemicals in your brain that affect your mood. Think of it like a mood thermostat — it helps keep your emotions from swinging too high or too low. Scientists believe it helps brain cells communicate more steadily, which leads to more stable moods over time.
common_side_effects: You may notice hand tremors (shakiness), increased thirst or urination, mild nausea, weight gain, or feeling a little tired or foggy, especially when you first start. Taking it with food can help with stomach upset. Many of these side effects get better as your body adjusts.
warnings: Lithium has a narrow safe range in your blood, so too much can become dangerous. Signs of too much lithium include severe tremors, confusion, slurred speech, vomiting, or feeling very unsteady — go to the ER right away if this happens. You will need regular blood tests to keep your lithium level safe. Staying well hydrated is very important, and avoid sudden changes in your salt intake since low salt can raise lithium levels. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with lithium.
typical_dosing: Lithium is usually taken 2 to 3 times a day with meals, though extended-release tablets (Lithobid) are often taken once or twice daily. Your doctor will start you at a low dose and adjust it based on your blood levels and how you feel. Most adults end up taking between 900 mg and 1200 mg per day, but your personal dose may be different. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
